cases.reason: A signed public event traversed three actual PWA bridge contexts and four independent Geode relays in the R1→R2→R3→R4 chain; each hop and the final inbox were independently reconciled.
Stopping P23 stopped new delivery at R2; restarting its PWA bridge replayed the eligible event through R3/R4. Age boundaries are covered separately with a fixed logical clock in G05-06.
Diamond, cycle and star topologies delivered through independent real browser bridges; relay ID queries showed one stored copy, and stopping one diamond path preserved delivery over the other.
Relay groups remained partitioned, then rejoined through a restarted P23. Two events published out of order reconciled once at R4 without duplicate IDs.

Three non-recipient bridge identities did not forward B’s envelope. B’s real PWA bridge forwarded only B’s recipient wrap to B’s inbox; A’s sender copy followed A’s inbox when A was the bridge identity.

UI toggle stopped and resumed the real PWA bridge. Fixed-input checks verified source exclusion, ID deduplication, signature/age boundaries, a 60-of-61 event batch and UTF-8 byte-based containment above 2 MB.

Closing the mobile-sized browser context stopped its bridge while both independent Geode relays remained available; a reopened context resumed forwarding. This is desktop viewport emulation only and does not certify physical mobile suspension/background behavior.

Two relay groups accepted conflicting signed updates while partitioned. The actual bridge reconciled them after reconnection, all relays selected the same NIP-01 tie winner independent of resolver input order, both append-only notes survived once, a later update superseded the conflict everywhere, and the marketplace UI rendered one valid card after each reconciliation.
